## The question

[Can someone help on this Markov Chain question?](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2065864/can-someone-help-on-this-markov-chain-question), asked by [Eoin](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/262423/eoin) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2016-12-20; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> Consider a general chain with state space $S = \left\{1, 2\right\}$ and write the
> transition matrix as
> $$P = \begin{pmatrix} 1-a & a \\ b & 1-b \end{pmatrix}$$
> Use the Markov property to show that
> $$\operatorname{Pr}\left\{X_{n+1} = 1\right\} − \frac{b}{a+b} 
>     = (1 − a − b)\left[\operatorname{Pr}\left\{X_n = 1\right\} − \frac{b}{a+b}\right]$$
> I'm using the fact that $p(1,1)=1-a$ and trying to equate this to $\operatorname{Pr}\left\{X_{n+1}=1\mid X_n=1\right\}$ to try and get $\operatorname{Pr}\left\{X_{n+1}=1\right\}$ and $\operatorname{Pr}\left\{X_n=1\right\}$ individually but I cant work it out.
:::

I guess you would want to use the fact that
$$\operatorname{Pr}\left\{X_{n+1}=1\right\} = \operatorname{Pr}\left\{X_{n+1}=1 \mid X_n=1\right\}\operatorname{Pr}\left\{X_n=1\right\}+\operatorname{Pr}\left\{X_{n+1} = 1 \mid X_n = 2\right\}(1-\operatorname{Pr}\left\{X_n=1)\right\}$$
and fill in the conditional probabilities from the transition matrix.
